cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Everything Has Two Prices
cards.instruction: Price every offer twice: once in practical terms and again through an emotional cost that grows when the offer returns.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. You can borrow the dress for ten pounds and an acknowledgment that you mocked it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Money covers fabric. It doesn't cover wearing my bad taste proudly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Now say which part of my judgement improved since yesterday.

mechanism: A turns its former dressmaking pupil borrowing fee into a growing emotional price: first admit mockery, then publicly credit the teacher taste.
confusable: Not only charging extra money or seeking one apology: additional cash cannot pay the second price, which grows when B offers a compliment.
comparison: Private delayed explanation versus public reversal of mockery.
